solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Be back in frills and checks

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other, here the turned word within the frills

parts.note: ruffs are frilled collars, so frills means ruffs

indicators.note: back means the little word Be is read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: An instruction to return, tangled up with frilly collars and checked fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'checks' looks like a fabric pattern beside frills, but it is the verb-turned-noun meaning setbacks or snubs.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebuff someone is to snub or repulse them, so rebuffs are checks in the sense of setbacks.

clue.text: With right hand, start to open letter from abroad

parts.note: H is an abbreviation for hand, as on watch dials and in card notation

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter of open is used

explanation.surface: Someone opening a letter sent from overseas, using their right hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Rho is the Greek letter for R, so it is a letter from a foreign alphabet.

clue.text: Belts or elastic support

indicators.note: something elastic can be stretched into a new shape, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Belts or elastic bands are described as forms of support for clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolster something is to prop it up or reinforce it, so it is a synonym of support.

clue.text: Not so many sheep kept by father

indicators.note: kept by means the sheep is held within the abbreviation for father

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
a ewe is a female sheep

explanation.surface: A father farmer whose flock has dwindled to just a few sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Fewer is the comparative of few, meaning a smaller number, i.e. not so many.

clue.text: Glorious, under tree

parts.note: sub is a Latin prefix meaning under, as in subway
the lime is a tree, also called the linden

explanation.surface: Lying under a tree on a glorious day.
explanation.definitionFit: Sublime describes something of awe-inspiring beauty or excellence, much like glorious.

clue.text: Part of sacred area

indicators.note: part of means the answer is a run of letters found within the word sacred

explanation.surface: A section of a holy site or sacred ground.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land measurement, so it is an area.

clue.text: Spy is a decent chap

parts.note: a gent, short for gentleman, is a decent, well-mannered chap

explanation.surface: Someone vouching that a suspected spy is really a decent fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent is an operative working for an intelligence service, i.e. a spy.

clue.text: Prince unhappy in the shade

parts.note: a prince is a royal, a member of a royal family
feeling blue means feeling sad or unhappy

explanation.surface: A prince sitting gloomily out of the sun in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shade' suggests shelter from the sun, but it means a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal blue is a deep vivid blue, a shade or hue of colour.

clue.text: In this industrial action, energy not very intelligent

parts.note: go means energy or drive, as in full of go
slow can mean dim-witted or not very bright

explanation.surface: A sneer that workers taking industrial action lack both energy and brains.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-slow is a protest in which workers deliberately work slowly, a form of industrial action.

clue.text: Cheers a couple of extras

definitions.meaning: cheers is informal British for goodbye
in cricket a bye is an extra, a run scored without the ball being hit

explanation.surface: A toast raised to a pair of extras, such as film walk-on actors.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, extras are runs not credited to a batsman, and byes are one kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheers is informal British for goodbye, just as bye-bye is a casual farewell.

clue.text: Writes to pal to arrange toy for child

indicators.note: to arrange letters is to put them into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone writing to a friend to organise a toy for a child.
explanation.definitionFit: A water pistol is a squirting plaything that children use for fun.

clue.text: Let lawmen loose with good intentions

indicators.note: let loose suggests letters set free to fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Releasing police officers onto the streets, supposedly with good motives.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-meant describes something done kindly, even if the result goes wrong.

clue.text: Wine tasting's beginning at Cambridge college

parts.note: Clare is one of the colleges of Cambridge University

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter of tasting is used

explanation.surface: A wine tasting held at a Cambridge college.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux, a type of wine.

clue.text: Those people without exception find the way to the Palace

definitions.meaning: read as ..., everyone in the group
The London road leading to Buckingham Palace

explanation.surface: Telling everyone, every last one, to find their way to the Palace.
explanation.walkthrough: The same letters split two ways: THEM ALL and THE MALL, the ceremonial London avenue running up to Buckingham Palace.
explanation.definitionFit: Them all means every one of those people; The Mall is the processional road to the Palace.

clue.text: Puff, no longer fit?

parts.note: ex means former, describing something that is no longer so
hale means healthy and fit, as in hale and hearty

explanation.surface: Someone out of puff who is no longer in good shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To puff is to blow out breath, which is what exhaling means.

clue.text: He provided the ultimate in escapist entertainment

definitions.text: He provided the ultimate in escapist entertainment

parts.words: He provided the ultimate in escapist entertainment
parts.note: escapist usually means fantasy entertainment, but here it is literal: a performer of daring escapes

explanation.surface: Praise for someone whose shows offered the best escape from reality.
explanation.walkthrough: Escapist entertainment normally means fantasy that lets audiences forget their troubles; here it means a stage act of escaping from chains and locked tanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Houdini was the most famous escape artist, freeing himself from handcuffs, straitjackets and sealed containers.

clue.text: What's taken in fun: computer device — ridiculously easy

parts.note: to take the mickey is to tease someone, so the mickey is what is taken in fun
a mouse is the hand-held pointing device for a computer

explanation.surface: A computer gadget mocked in jest as absurdly simple to use.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the mickey is British slang for making fun of someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Mickey Mouse is informal for trivially simple or amateurish, as in a Mickey Mouse course.

clue.text: Damage after cold spell

indicators.note: after means the damage word follows the letter for cold

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
to harm something is to damage it

explanation.surface: Damage done following a spell of cold weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spell' looks like a period of weather but means a magic incantation.
explanation.definitionFit: A charm is a magic incantation or spell meant to bring about an effect.

clue.text: Quantity missing initial rise

indicators.note: missing initial means the synonym loses its first letter

parts.note: an amount is a quantity

explanation.surface: A quantity that fails to show its first rise.
explanation.definitionFit: To mount is to climb or go up, so it means to rise.

clue.text: Airline that collapsed beside a canal

indicators.note: beside means the letter a is placed next to the airline

parts.note: Pan Am was a major US airline that went bankrupt in 1991

explanation.surface: An airline that went bust alongside a canal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Panama Canal links the Atlantic and Pacific oceans across Central America.

clue.text: Marriages showing problems afoot? Not the first

indicators.note: not the first means the synonym loses its opening letter

parts.note: bunions are painful swellings on the foot, literally problems on foot

explanation.surface: Marriages that seem to have trouble brewing, though not the first one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'afoot' suggests something in progress but here means on the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A union is a marriage, the joining of two people in wedlock.

clue.text: Sister nobody's spoken of

indicators.note: spoken of means the answer sounds like the word for nobody

parts.note: none means not one, nobody

explanation.surface: A sister nobody ever mentions.
explanation.definitionFit: A nun is a member of a religious order, addressed as Sister.

clue.text: Scrap a vehicle test requiring reversing

indicators.note: reversing means the test's abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for vehicles in Britain

explanation.surface: A car facing the scrapheap needs a vehicle test that involves reversing.
explanation.walkthrough: MOT is the compulsory yearly British road-safety check, named after the Ministry of Transport.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom is a tiny piece, so it can mean a scrap, as in not an atom of truth.

clue.text: Reluctant to join Scotsman in part of his country

parts.note: loth means unwilling or reluctant
Ian is a typically Scottish name, standing for a Scotsman

explanation.surface: A Scotsman reluctant to join something in his own land.
explanation.walkthrough: Lothian is a region of Scotland around Edinburgh; 'his' refers back to the Scotsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Lothian is a historic region of Scotland, the Scotsman's own country.
